h1: Cabinet Refinishing in Fort White, FL
heroIntro: Painted kitchen and bath cabinets for Fort White homes, finished with a hard enamel that handles humid kitchens. You keep your layout and get a new look.

questions: Do painted cabinets peel in humid Florida homes?
What's the difference between cabinet refinishing and replacement?
How do you fix cabinet paint that is already peeling?

body: Kitchens in older ranch homes and riverfront houses deal with steam, damp air, and a lot of hand contact. Cheap cabinet paint gets tacky, chips at the edges, and peels near the sink and dishwasher. Cabinet refinishing in Fort White, FL uses a system designed for that: thorough degreasing, a bonding primer that grips factory finishes, and a waterborne urethane enamel that cures much harder than wall paint.

sections.h2: When a previous paint job failed
body: We often see cabinets someone painted with wall paint and no primer. That finish has to come off, or at least be sanded back to a sound surface, before a new system can bond. If yours are already flaking, our article on a temporary fix for peeling cabinet paint can hold you over until the walkthrough. Deciding whether the boxes are worth keeping? Read refinish vs. replace.

bullets: Remove and label doors, drawer fronts, and hardware
Fill dings and open grain if you want it smooth
Bonding primer, then two coats of urethane enamel
Reinstall, adjust doors, and walk through the finish with you
body: Colors can be matched from a chip, a sample door, or a leftover can, and you approve a full-size drawdown before we spray. Low-VOC options are available.

Grain is a matter of taste. Oak cabinets, common in older Fort White kitchens, have open grain that shows through paint unless it is filled. Some owners like a little texture, and others want a smooth, factory-style look. We show you both on a sample before committing. Hardware can be reused or swapped during reassembly, and we adjust hinges so doors close evenly. Every door goes back in the opening it came from.

Cabinets can be done any time of year. Most projects start one to three weeks after approval, and the estimate lays out when the kitchen will be affected. The walkthrough is free and usually happens within 48 hours, with a crew lead looking at the boxes, doors, and any old finish. Many owners paint the kitchen walls at the same time. See interior painting in Fort White for that. The full service is on our cabinet painting and refinishing page, and you can return to the Fort White contractor page for other local work.

faqs.q: Will painted cabinets hold up in a humid Fort White kitchen?
faqs.a: With proper degreasing, a bonding primer, and a waterborne urethane enamel, yes. That system cures hard and resists moisture.

faqs.q: Can you fix cabinets someone else painted badly?
faqs.a: Yes. Failing paint is removed or sanded back to a sound surface before the new primer and enamel go on.
